sentences.text: Apprehending the arrest at the hands of police in connection with Crime No.370/2023 registered with Police Station Ballarsha, District Chandrapur for the offence punishable under Section 420 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, the applicant approached this Court for grant of pre-arrest bail.

2. As per the allegation in the FIR which is registered on the basis of report lodged by the informant namely Rahim Ayyub Khan that he had completed his diploma Course in Mining Engineering and was in search of job since 2021.
His father's friend namely Harish Deorao Khobragade informed his father that he is acquainted with one person namely Vignoj Rajurkar resident of Rajura, who could arrange the job for the complainant.

As such on 06.02.2021, the complainant along with his father and Harish Khobragade went to Chandrapur to meet (2) 913.aba.265.2024 Vignoj Rajurkar where another person namely Anup Bele was also present.

During meeting with the co-accused who told his father that he is having good relations with officer of head office of WCL Nagpur and the complainant is required to pay Rs.20,00,000/- then he could try to get a job as Operator in WCL.
It is further alleged that thereafter, they meet the present applicant and present applicant also promised him for the job.
It is alleged that complainant had paid the amount of Rs.5,00,000/- by way of cheque to the co-accused.
On the basis of the said report, police have registered the crime against the present applicant as well as other co-accused.
3. It is submitted by the learned Counsel for the applicant that the applicant is neither beneficiary nor he is related with any of the activities committed by the co-accused.
Merely on suspicion the offence is registered against him.
As far as the custodial interrogation of the present applicant is Someshwar Tulsiram Yelchalwar vs The State Of Maharashtra Thr.

Considering that he has not received any amount, in view of that,
he be protected by granting ad-interim anticipatory bail.

4. Learned APP strongly opposed the said application on the ground that the huge amount was paid by the informant for securing the job which was not given to him and the amount is to be recovered from the present applicant as well as from the (3) 913.aba.265.2024 co-accused, therefore custodial interrogation is required.
5. Having heard the learned Counsel for the applicant and the learned APP for the State, perused the recitals of the FIR.

There is specific allegation against the present applicant in the FIR that the complainant and his father met the present applicant, at the relevant time present applicant has also assured them about the job and thereafter, they have paid the amount.
Admittedly, the alleged offence registered is punishable with imprisonment upto seven years.
The Investigating Officer has to follow the mandatory provisions i.e. notice under Section 41 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Section 41 under Chapter V of the Code deals with the arrest of persons.
Even for a cognizable offence, an arrest is not mandatory as can be seen from the mandate of this provision.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureu of Investigation and another reported in 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 577 wherein it is observed that if the officer is satisfied that a person has committed a cognizable offence, punishable with imprisonment for a term which may be less than seven years, or which may extend to the said period, with or without fine, an arrest could only follow when he is satisfied that there is a reason to believe or suspect, that the said person has committed an offence, and there is a necessity for an arrest.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureu of Investigation and another reported in 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 577
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Such necessity is drawn to prevent the (4)
913.aba.265.2024 committing of any further offence, for a proper investigation, and to prevent him/her from either disappearing or tampering with the evidence.

He/she can also be arrested to prevent such person from making any inducement, threat, or promise to any person according to the facts, so as to dissuade him from disclosing said facts either to the court or to the police officer.
This provision mandates the police officer to record his reasons in writing while making the arrest.
Thus, a police officer is duty-bound to record the reasons for arrest in writing.
Similarly, the police officer shall record reasons when he/she chooses not to arrest.
The consequence of non-compliance with Section 41 shall certainly inure to the benefit of the person suspected of the offence.
6. In view of the observations of the Hon'ble Apex Court, in the present case, as offence punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code is less than seven years.
In view of that, the Investigating Officer shall follow the guidelines issued by the Hon'ble Apex Court by recording the reasons why arrest of the present applicant is required.

As far as the allegations are concerned, at this stage, no case is made out for grant of ad-interim protection.
7. Stand over after one week.
(URMILA JOSHI-PHALKE, J.) Sarkate
